subject: Transience policy Q: what we keep by default (requests vs derived outputs)

Subject: Quick Q on what Redwood keeps by default (requests vs derivatives)

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. One thing that came up internally: can you clarify Redwood's default behavior for storing request/response content (prompts, user messages) versus derived artifacts (summaries, embeddings, logs)? Neptune needs to understand what is captured by default for our security & data governance team.

Specifics we need:
- Does Redwood store raw prompts and model outputs by default on the hosted API? For how long?
- Are embeddings or other derived artifacts treated the same as outputs?
- If we need a shorter retention window or on-demand purge for a subset of sessions, what is the workflow and SLA?

Appreciate a concise breakdown we can share with our compliance team.

Best,
Alex
Alex Moreno
Senior Platform Engineer, Neptune Analytics


From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 13:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Quick Q on what Redwood keeps by default (requests vs derivatives)

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear questions. High-level first, then concrete next steps.

Summary (hosted API defaults):
- Request/response content (prompts & model outputs): retained by default for 30 days. This allows us to power retries, debugging, and quality monitoring.
- Derived artifacts (embeddings, reranks, indexed summaries): retained separately; default retention is 90 days for embedding indexes and 30 days for ephemeral derivatives unless configured otherwise.
- Telemetry & aggregated logs (latency, token counts, error traces): retained for 365 days by default (used for billing/observability).

Key exceptions & controls:
- Private and Dedicated customers control retention via their config/contract. For Private deployments the default is customer-managed (we do not centrally retain content unless explicitly enabled).
- Customers can enable prompt-only opt-out at project-level (prompts never persisted) — this is a per-project flag; when set, model outputs can still be retained unless output-persistence is also disabled.
- Immediate deletion requests: we offer an ad-hoc purge flow (see attached sample_purge_playbook.pdf). For hosted API, deletion requests are queued and processed with tombstone propagation; standard SLA for full propagation is up to 5 business days for content index and 10 business days for derived artifact cleanup.

Practical examples:
- If you call the hosted API today without any opt-outs, the raw request and generated text will be available to you via the console for 30 days, then removed. Embeddings generated as part of that call will be retained 90 days in the default embedding index.

Next steps I propose:
1) Kimberly (security) — can you confirm if the SLA above is appropriate for Neptune's ATO process?
2) Alex — if you want a pilot with prompt-only opt-out and a 7-day retention window for outputs, we can spin up a trial project and run the purge-playbook against it.
3) I'll attach the policy doc and SOC2 summary for legal review.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min sync if helpful.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Quick Q on what Redwood keeps by default (requests vs derivatives)

Adding a quick security-side clarification.

- Classification: we treat prompts and outputs as "customer content" for retention and deletion purposes. That means delete requests remove both request payloads and model outputs from our hosted stores, subject to the purge workflow described below.
- Purge mechanics: deletion creates a tombstone entry; the content is removed from active indexes and backups are scheduled for cleanup during the next retention-rotation (within the SLA Hannah noted). Some long-term forensic backups (for SOC/incident investigations) are retained in encrypted form but are inaccessible except under legal/incident review and are removed per our backup retention policy (we provide customers attestations).
- Derived artifacts nuance: embeddings and derivative indexes may be sharded or replicated across storage tiers. Purge will mark and remove shards but full convergence across replicas can take the up-to-10-business-day window.

Action items for sales/CS:
- If Neptune requires an auditable deletion timeline shorter than 10 business days we need an exception routed through our renewals/enterprise ops team (this is doable under an SLA amendment).
- I'll attach the SOC2_Audit_Summary.pdf that documents how backups and forensic snapshots are handled.

Kimberly Park
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
